src: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (Swedish: Nobelpriset i fysiologi eller medicin) is awarded annually by the Karolinska Swedish Institute to scientists and physicians in various fields of physiology or medicine. src: Papia or Pavia is a city in northern Italy in the Lombardy region, capital of the province of Papia, located on the Ticcino River, north of its confluence with the Paddy River, 35 km south of Milan, dating back to the Roman era under the name Ticinum, it was the capital of the Lombard Kingdom. In the Middle Ages it was the seat of one of Italy's most prestigious universities. The city remained fortified until 1872 when the fortresses were converted into public streets and gardens, but the largest part of the walls remained until 1901 when it was demolished to build cobblestone streets, incorporating many tourist and cultural symbols, and renowned for its landscapes, particularly grapes, vineyards, vineyards, and vineyards.

src: It appears that the use of the crown called for another thing, that the man in ancient times was after working to gain his power inclined to rest. He covered his face from the heat of the sun with a crown he took from the herbs he shaved and surrounded his head. He used this type of crown most often when eating. Hence the tendency to wear a crown at meals and make a title of comfort and reassurance of the heart. Hence the crowning of the gods at the heathen originated. The Greeks crowned the god Jupiter the Great with a crown composed of all the flowers signifying his authority over all the gods and crowned each god of the gods who followed with a crown according to the functions they were engaged in plotting this world.

src: Almakha was chiefly worshipped in the slave capital of Ma'rib, where thousands of inscriptions were presented to him in the Temple of Awam (popularly called: Mahram Bil-Kis), as well as in the Temple of Owal-Siroah (Almakha Temple) in the center of the ancient city of Ma'rib, alongside other temples such as the Temple of Harun (which built the Mosque of Solomon on its ruins), and the Temple of Baran (popularly called: Throne of Balqis or A'maid Balqis) outside the ancient city of Ma'rib, and a large pilgrimage ceremony and procession was held for him between the Temple of Awam and Ma'rib; these various temples were mixed in heritage because of the king's connection with the mythological and Islamic heritage in Ma'rib.

src: National Geographic Kids is an American monthly popular science children's magazine published by the National Geographic Society in September 1975 under the name National Geographic World. The magazine was published for 26 years under that name before being renamed National Geographic Kids in October 2001. src: Foodborne illness or food poisoning is a group of symptoms resulting from eating food contaminated with bacteria, or toxins produced by these organisms. Food poisoning also results from eating food contaminated with various types of viruses, germs, parasites, and toxic chemicals such as mushroom poisoning.
